title: C# Questions & Answers - Operation on Characters
sourceFile: Characters Operation - C# Questions & Answers - Sanfoundry.html
description: This section of our 1000+ C# multiple choice questions focuses on operation of characters in C# Programming Language.

questions.question: Which property of the String class gives the number of characters in a string?
questions.explanation: In C#, 'Length' is a property of the String class (not a method) used to get the number of characters in the string.

questions.question: Which method is commonly used to encode a string into a byte array?
questions.explanation: The 'Encoding.GetBytes()' method (from System.Text) converts a string into a byte array based on a specific encoding.

questions.question: Which of these methods converts all characters of a string into a character array?
questions.explanation: The 'ToCharArray()' method copies the characters in a string to a Unicode character array.

questions.question: Which StringBuilder method completes the following C# code?
questions.explanation: The 'Append()' method of StringBuilder adds a string to the end of the current StringBuilder object.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: 'IndexOf' returns the first occurrence index. 'l' is at index 3. 'LastIndexOf' returns the last occurrence index. 'o' is at index 5 (love) and 9 (you), so it returns 9. 'e' is at index 6.

questions.question: Which of these String methods is used to delete characters from a string?
questions.explanation: The 'Remove()' method returns a new string in which a specified number of characters in the current string have been deleted.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code snippet?
questions.explanation: Remove(1) deletes every character from index 1 through the end. Only the character at index 0 ('h') remains.

questions.question: How is a string typically processed in low-level character operations?

options.text: On a character by character basis
On a string by string basis
Both On a character by character basis & On a string by string basis

questions.explanation: Strings are essentially sequences of characters, and many operations (like searching or parsing) process them one character at a time.

questions.question: How do you print two backslash characters \\ on the console in C#?
questions.explanation: In C#, the backslash is an escape character. To print one backslash, you need two '\\'. To print two backslashes, you need four '\\\\'.
